title: Unlinking Multiple Inputs
goal: Disentangle lifetimes when a function only borrows from one input.

sections.text: You use multiple lifetime parameters when a function borrows from several inputs independently.

sections.caption: 'a ties the output to x, while _y uses 'b.

sections.text: Giving both arguments the same lifetime parameter forces the compiler to treat both inputs as borrowed for as long as the returned reference lives.
Giving `_y` a separate lifetime parameter `'b` lets the caller drop or mutate `_y` while keeping the reference to `x`.
Rust requires you to specify this when elision cannot determine which input is being returned.

explanation: Disentangle lifetimes when a function only borrows from one input.
